group.passage:
Entertainers and their fans are mutually reliant, and the creation of fan clubs solidifies the bond between them. Just as Benedict Cumberbatch lovingly nicknames his fans “Cumberbabes,” Lady Gaga calls [[1]] Little Monsters. K-Pop groups, on the other hand, have fanbases that proudly give themselves such names that not only demonstrate their loyalty but also [[2]]: “Don’t mess with my idols.” That is, these fandoms’ devotion to their idols takes the form of aggressiveness. BTS’ ARMY and BLACKPINK’s Blinks are known to have launched attacks on people who cast their favorite artists in a(n) [[3]] light.
In 2020, ARMY drowned the TWITTER account of the Royal Ballet with vicious comments after the latter made a joke about Black Swan, a new single by BTS. In 2022, the musical comedy duo TwoSet Violin [[4]] a storm of hate comments from BLACKPINK fans after creating Sell Out, a musical parody of BLACKPINK’s Shut Down. Some Blinks even flooded the TWITTER account of Singapore Symphony Orchestra, demanding their upcoming concert with TwoSet be canceled. Some people criticize such fandom as toxic. True, no one likes to see their favorite artists [[5]] in any way, but being protective doesn’t give anyone the right to harass or insult others. Truth be told, such verbal aggression isn’t exactly doing their idols any favor.

tags.topic: aggressive K-pop fandoms attacking critics of their idols
